intents: Configure ISAV-style anti-spoofing on fw to block amplification/reflection traffic arriving from the WAN with a spoofed LAN source.
wan is connected to fw eth1 on 198.51.100.0/24.
lan is connected to fw eth2 on 10.10.20.0/24.
Keep legitimate forwarding from wan to lan working.
Drop traffic entering fw eth1 if its IPv4 source belongs to the protected LAN prefix 10.10.20.0/24.
Enable strict reverse-path filtering on fw eth1 as an additional anti-spoofing signal.
Do not modify IP addressing or management connectivity on eth0.

fw: nft add chain inet isav forward '{ type filter hook forward priority -10; policy accept; }'
nft add rule inet isav forward iifname "eth1" ip saddr 10.10.20.0/24 counter drop

ground_truth_reasoning: ISAV/anti-amplification filtering should be placed on the WAN ingress side. Legitimate WAN traffic has a source reachable via fw eth1, while packets entering eth1 with a source from the protected LAN prefix are spoofed and should be dropped before forwarding. The nftables forward-hook rule enforces the ACL, and strict rp_filter on eth1 adds a kernel-level reverse-path check without changing the data-plane addressing.

baseline_invariants.name: WAN management interface is still up
FW management interface is still up
LAN management interface is still up

testcases.name: Legitimate WAN to LAN ICMP still works
Spoofed LAN-source probe from WAN receives no replies
ISAV ACL is installed on the forward path
Strict rp_filter is enabled on WAN interface
